newsitem.title: KENYA: WFP reports 100,000 Hutu refugees on the move.
newsitem.headline: WFP reports 100,000 Hutu refugees on the move.

text.p: - The World Food Programme (WFP) reported "strong indications" that at least 100,000 Hutu refugees still in eastern Zaire were on the move on Wednesday.

"There are strong indications that a large movement of people from the Bukavu area are heading north towards Goma. We believe there could be more than 100,000," WFP spokeswoman Michele Quintaglie said in Nairobi.
Quintaglie said she was not yet authorised to say how the WFP knew the refugees were walking northwards.

If confirmed, the WFP report would clear the mystery about the whereabouts of some of the estimated 700,000 Hutus still in Zaire since 500,000 others walked back into Rwanda from Goma between November 15 and 19.
There was no firm news of the intended destination of the 100,000 people on the move, Quintaglie said.
But if they intend to go back into Rwanda "we think the influx could begin arriving as early as tomorrow but definitely between the next one to two days," she told Reuters.
